Say I have an app with two tabs and a sidebar. The sidebar has an actionButton which triggers some analysis within an eventReactive expression. The analysis can take a couple of minutes to process.
The result of the eventReactive expression is rendered as an output on Tab A. Tab B displays no output.
When I have a Tab A selected and click the actionButton, the analysis is triggered immediately.
When I have a Tab B selected and click the actionButton, nothing happens, until I switch to Tab A when the analysis is then triggered.
I would like the analysis to be triggered when the actionButton is clicked regardless of which tab is selected.
My workaround is for the eventReactive expression to also output a blank string which is rendered as output on Tab B.

My actual app has eight tabs so I need to render and output multiple blank strings. Is there a better solution to this?

Thanks

Philip Perrin

messages.subject: Dealing with nested selectizeInputs and reactivity
messages.subject_clean: Dealing with nested selectizeInputs and reactivity
messages.body_plain:
Hey folks,

I am having trouble with nested selectizeInputs, i.e. a group of select inputs where the selection in the first determines the choices in the second, which control the choices in the third, and so on.

Let's say I have an select1 that lets you choose a dataset, and select2 which lets you pick a variable in the dataset. Obviously the choices in select2 depend on the selection in select1. I find that if a user selects a variable from select2, and then changes select1, it doesn't immediately wipe out the value from select2, but instead it goes through a reactive sequence with the new value in select1, and the old value from select2, which is suddenly referencing a variable in a different dataset, which is a problem.

Example:

library(shiny)

ui =fluidPage(
  selectizeInput('d',choices=c('mtcars','iris'),
                 label="Datasets"),
  uiOutput("vars"),
  htmlOutput("out")
)

server = function(input, output, session) {

  output$vars <- renderUI({
    req(input$d)
    selectizeInput("v",choices=names(get(input$d)), label="Variables",
                   options=list(onInitialize=I('function() {this.setValue("");}')
  })

  output$out <- renderUI({
    req(input$d,input$v)
    HTML(paste0("The max is ",max(get(input$d)[[input$v]])))
  })

}
runApp(list(ui = ui, server = server))

On launch, select mpg, and displays max value.

Now, after selecting mpg, if you switch to iris, you will get a barely noticeable error, then it corrects itself. This is a toy example, so the error is insignificant, but there could easily be cases where the error is much more dire (as is the case with the app I am currently developing).

Is there a way to handle nested selectizeInputs such that changes in an upstream selectizeInput won't evaluate with old values of down stream selectizeInputs when changed?

Thanks

messages.subject_clean: How to run long R Scripts with Shiny
messages.body_plain:
Hi Laz,

I totally took your input and now just use shiny to save the user files/parameters to the server. Once shiny copies the files over, shiny is done with.

I ended up not running cron though.  On the sever, I just crated an R script that is constantly running using nohup, to check to see if the "Jobs To Complete" folder has a new job to run.

If a job exists, the script moves the file [with the oldest date] to a a folder called, "In process", calls the main R script that processes the files, and then sends an email to the user once it's completed. If the job failed, it sends the user the stdrr file. Finally, the script moves these files to a "completed" folder, and the loop starts over to process the next job.

Thank you so much for your help and input!

On Fri, Oct 28, 2016 at 7:12 PM, Laz C. Peterson <l...@paravis.net> wrote:
> Hey there Shelley --
>
> Your users could have (for example) access to some network share or somewhere on the server that they could save their files. And your script could start (before the Rscript part) by doing a "find" command for any files sitting in that folder. That's just an idea ... but you could definitely have it run on a single cron job.
>
> Either make sure their data gets stored as a file in a specific location on the server, or I would recommend setting up a MySQL server and then using DbWriteTable (or is it DbCopyTable?) functions to just throw it into the database server. Much easier accessed that way.
>
> If your front end app could simply accept their data and place it as a file on the server or into a database, the cron script could run and just check those locations for anything that needs to be processed. You'll just need a way of defining which user is waiting for the results from which files - either putting this information as metadata inside the file name, or having a database table linked with that information. That's a discussion we could have another time. (If you're interested in the database method, I can explain how we do ours in private emails.)
>
> The big issue you're facing is making sure that if they do not wait for processing to finish before closing their browser, the data could go into the oblivion. So to have a reliable system, it will definitely have to have a few moving parts. A Shiny front end is great, with a cron-style R back end.
>
> We used to have our data stored as files, but the more you work with, the harder it is to deal with. Databases are great because we can index each dataset and flag it as new, processed, processed but not reported yet, etc.
>
> Learning dplyr, DBI and pool package functions will get you sorted proper with the database input and output.
>
> It's been a long week, so I'm probably not making any sense at this point ha ha. But feel free to ask any questions you like.
>
> Have a great weekend.

messages.subject: Re: How to run long R Scripts with Shiny
messages.subject_clean: How to run long R Scripts with Shiny
messages.body_plain:
Rock on, sounds like you have it sorted out!

One thing to pay special attention to, just ensure that your background script has some way of verifying that the file is 100% finished being copied over from the client.  I am not sure how to do that properly in R, (or even bash script for that matter).  But on our Windows servers, the easy test we use to check if a file has finished being written is a “copy file.txt+NUL file.txt >NUL” … And if it errors out saying “The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process.”  I think linux shell scripts are a little more involved to work with checking file access.

We’ve had to deal with that issue, where users' data files were being moved prematurely, or causing issues with the scripts.  So just make sure that your setup is good to go in that regard.

Cheers.

~ Laz Peterson
Paravis, LLC

> On Nov 1, 2016, at 8:38 PM, Shelley MacNeil <smacn...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi Laz,
>
> I totally took your input and now just use shiny to save the user files/parameters to the server. Once shiny copies the files over, shiny is done with.
>
> I ended up not running cron though.  On the sever, I just crated an R script that is constantly running using nohup, to check to see if the "Jobs To Complete" folder has a new job to run.
>
> If a job exists, the script moves the file [with the oldest date] to a a folder called, "In process", calls the main R script that processes the files, and then sends an email to the user once it's completed. If the job failed, it sends the user the stdrr file. Finally, the script moves these files to a "completed" folder, and the loop starts over to process the next job.
>
> Thank you so much for your help and input!
>
>
>
>
>
> On Fri, Oct 28, 2016 at 7:12 PM, Laz C. Peterson <l...@paravis.net> wrote:
> > Hey there Shelley --
> >
> > Your users could have (for example) access to some network share or somewhere on the server that they could save their files. And your script could start (before the Rscript part) by doing a "find" command for any files sitting in that folder. That's just an idea ... but you could definitely have it run on a single cron job.
> >
> > Either make sure their data gets stored as a file in a specific location on the server, or I would recommend setting up a MySQL server and then using DbWriteTable (or is it DbCopyTable?) functions to just throw it into the database server. Much easier accessed that way.
> >
> > If your front end app could simply accept their data and place it as a file on the server or into a database, the cron script could run and just check those locations for anything that needs to be processed. You'll just need a way of defining which user is waiting for the results from which files - either putting this information as metadata inside the file name, or having a database table linked with that information. That's a discussion we could have another time. (If you're interested in the database method, I can explain how we do ours in private emails.)
> >
> > The big issue you're facing is making sure that if they do not wait for processing to finish before closing their browser, the data could go into the oblivion. So to have a reliable system, it will definitely have to have a few moving parts. A Shiny front end is great, with a cron-style R back end.
> >
> > We used to have our data stored as files, but the more you work with, the harder it is to deal with. Databases are great because we can index each dataset and flag it as new, processed, processed but not reported yet, etc.
> >
> > Learning dplyr, DBI and pool package functions will get you sorted proper with the database input and output.
> >
> > It's been a long week, so I'm probably not making any sense at this point ha ha. But feel free to ask any questions you like.
> >
> > Have a great weekend.

I have a shiny app with a really long page, and I would like to create an actionButton that allows user to go directly to one particular reactiveObject.

As I already programed in html I thought about href and local anchor.

For a text no problem, I would add an href = "#Object" to the a() (http://stackoverflow.com/questions/28605185/create-link-to-the-other-part-of-the-shiny-app), but for an actionButton, I can not figure out how to do that (perhaps with a div?).

Here is my code for an reproducible example:

library(shiny)

runApp(
  # Ui
  list(ui = pageWithSidebar(
    headerPanel("Test App"),

    sidebarPanel(
      div(actionButton("Go", "Go to the Button"), href ="#try" )),

              br(),
              uiOutput("try")
              )
  ),

  # Server
  server = function(input, output, session) {

    output$try <- renderUI({
      actionButton("Well", "well done!")

))

Do you have any idea for doing that ?

Cheers

messages.subject: DataTable not rendering when contained inside hidden div
messages.subject_clean: DataTable not rendering when contained inside hidden div
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

We have a dataTableOutput() contained within a tags$div with style=‘display:none;’, which is toggled to display on and off by a button.  Everything works as expected, except for the actual table itself.  It is never rendered by the server.

If we remove the style, it renders just fine.

We have tried outputOptions() with suspendWhenHidden=FALSE, but that does not help.

Is there something I’m missing about the way Shiny works that would break the renderDataTable() function when sending to a hidden div?

Any thoughts?

~ Laz Peterson
Paravis, LLC

messages.subject_clean: DataTable not rendering when contained inside hidden div
messages.body_plain:
Yihui, do you possibly have some insight to this?

~~~~ code ~~~~

library(shiny)
library(DT)

ui<-fluidPage(
    tags$div(style='text-align:center;',tags$button(type='button',onClick='$("#hiddenDiv").fadeIn();',class='btn btn-primary','Unhide Element')),
    fluidRow(
        column(6,tags$div(id='hiddenDiv',style='display:none;',tags$p('Hidden Table'),dataTableOutput('hiddenTable'))),
        column(6,tags$div(id='regularDiv',tags$p('Visible Table'),dataTableOutput('regularTable')))
    )
)
server<-function(input,output,session){
    output$hiddenTable<-renderDataTable({
        thisData<-data.frame(a=sample(1:10),b=sample(1:10),c=sample(1:10))
        datatable(thisData)
    })
    outputOptions(output,'hiddenTable',suspendWhenHidden=FALSE)
    output$regularTable<-renderDataTable({
        thisData<-data.frame(a=sample(1:10),b=sample(1:10),c=sample(1:10))
        datatable(thisData)
    })
}
shinyApp(ui,server)

~~~~ end code ~~~~

The hidden div does not receive the dataTableOutput ... Is there a more appropriate way to accomplish this task?

Thank you!
~Laz Peterson
Paravis, LLC

messages.subject: Re: Shiny and parallel processing
messages.subject_clean: Shiny and parallel processing
messages.body_plain:
Any thoughts on this one, Joe?  (Hopefully the RDS file containing the data we use with HTML() made it to your inbox ok?)

We have this gift app that builds each respective gift giver's (5 individuals) tiles based on only the live data that applies to them (roughly 150 average for each person).  So, there really is no way to do it statically.

And then there is an administrative gift user, who gets tiles of all of the gift givers (an aggregated total of about 300).

So the more tiles we create, the processing time increases exponentially.  I'm sure there is a better way to accomplish this task, but I'm at a loss.

If the HTML output performance from the server side worked as fast as the native Shiny functions, I would probably run around in circles for joy.  It would increase our possibilities infinitely, and I would actually start rebuilding each of our Javascript/PHP apps to be built on Shiny's framework.

Much thanks for your insight.
~Laz Peterson
Paravis, LLC

messages.body_plain:
I think that was due to
https://github.com/rstudio/DT/blob/aad518c5b/inst/htmlwidgets/datatables.js#L73
The intention here was to hold rendering until the table becomes
visible: https://github.com/rstudio/DT/blob/aad518c5b/inst/htmlwidgets/datatables.js#L864
Well, other than "becoming visible", one of these events has to be
triggered: https://github.com/ramnathv/htmlwidgets/blob/7454758379/inst/www/htmlwidgets.js#L582-L600
In your case, perhaps none of the events were triggered when you click
the button. I don't know what the best way to trigger the event is,
but perhaps you need to do something like $(window).trigger('resize');
when clicking the button. I'm sorry that you have to hack at this
using JavaScript, but I don't see an alternative way at the moment.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Removing multiple elements with removeUI

messages.body_plain:
I was suggested using insertUI here <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/40430899/how-to-retain-sliderinput-range-of-a-variables-when-additional-variables-added?noredirect=1#comment68153429_40430899> and found that it as a great feature. The following code allows to generate control widgets for a single or multiple elements using insertUI, but struck on incorporating removeUI related part. Tried jQuery options to remove inserted UI elements but did not work out. I found the following from Shiny dynamic UI <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/dynamic-ui.html>, i.e., Note that, if you are inserting multiple elements in one call, you must wrap them in either a tagList() or a tags$div() (the latter option has the advantage that you can give it an id to make it easier to reference or remove it later on). Also, comments here <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/40430899/how-to-retain-sliderinput-range-of-a-variables-when-additional-variables-added?noredirect=1#comment68153429_40430899> gave some clues, i.e., tags$div(id="sepal.width.div", sliderInput("sepal.width.slider", ...)), but my lack of HTML/CSS knowledge stops me going forward. I'm looking at (a) wrapping multiple widget element(s) with tags$div() assigning a unique id for each variable, which will be used in removeUI; (b) calling multiple elements via removeUI.

varnames <- names(iris[,1:4]) # names
varinit <- apply(iris[,1:4],2,median) # initival value used in slider
varmin <- apply(iris[,1:4],2,min) # min.
varmax <- apply(iris[,1:4],2,max) # max.

ListofSelVars <<- vector(mode="character")

# control widgets for all elements
allControls <- lapply(setNames(varnames, varnames), function(x) {

   sliderInput(x, x, varmin[x], varmax[x], c(varmin[x], varinit[x]),
               round = -2)
})

ui <- navbarPage(
   tabPanel("Plot",
            sidebarLayout(
               sidebarPanel(
                  checkboxGroupInput("ConditioningVariables", "Conditioning variables (choose one or more):",
                                     varnames,inline = TRUE),
                  # add an action button
                  actionButton("add", "Update UI elements")
               ),
               mainPanel()
            )
   )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
   observeEvent(input$add, {
      insertUI(
         selector ='#add',
         where = "afterEnd",
         ui = allControls[setdiff(input$ConditioningVariables,ListofSelVars)]
      )

      ## removeUI related goes, here
      ## removeUI(selector=paste0())
      ## setdiff(ListofSelVars,input$ConditioningVariables) gives elements to be removed

      ## Global variable, keep track of elements that are selected

      ListofSelVars <<- input$ConditioningVariables

   })

}
shinyApp(ui, server)

messages.subject: How to I put a link on an R Shiny histogram bin so that I can open a second R Shiny application?
messages.subject_clean: How to I put a link on an R Shiny histogram bin so that I can open a second R Shiny application?
messages.body_plain:
Master/Detail:

I really am a rank beginner with R and Shiny, but I've been asked to write a proof of concept report (graph) to see if we should switch to this platform. So, I've bought a book and started looking at examples I've found on the web, but I hope someone can point me in the right direction for documentation on a good approach to the problem I've been set.

We would like to have a master/detail report.

In the master report, the user is presented with a histogram. Click on a histogram bin and a window opens with the detail report.

Specifically, we are reporting deaths by county (US) by day in the histogram master. When the user clicks on one of the counties (one of the histogram bins), they should be presented with a list of death records for that county for that day.

We'd like to know how hard it would be to do a report of this type in R Shiny. I am hoping that someone can point me to a specific example of R that does something similar or to the documentation I should look at for what I am trying to do.

I'd imagine something like a link on each county bin, but I could not see a way to do that using the hist() function.

messages.body_plain:
Here's a stripped down example of a master/detail view:
https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/2e790a8570c84917c86c1a99f33ba548

You'll first need to install shiny, ggplot2 and DT:
install.packages(c("shiny", "ggplot2", "DT"))

Then you can run it with:
shiny::runGist("https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/2e790a8570c84917c86c1a99f33ba548")

I wouldn't necessarily say this is particularly advanced Shiny code, but you will need to know a bit about reactive programming to understand it.
https://www.rstudio.com/resources/webinars/shiny-developer-conference/ (Effective Reactive Programming parts 1 and 2)

Handling the actual plot clicks is the interactive plots feature; you'll find the first in a series of three articles here:
http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/plot-interaction.html

The trickiest bit will be having it open "in a new window". Shiny is currently designed for "single page applications" (SPA) so it's not natural to have two separate pages as part of the same app. However there's several options to deal with that.

Don't actually open a new window, just have it load in the same page, as I have in this example.
Use tabsetPanel <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/tabsets.html> or navbarPage <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/layout-guide.html#navbar-pages> to separate the two views but still have them on the same page
Use modal dialogs <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/modal-dialogs.html> for the detail view
There are techniques you can use to get Shiny to render multiple pages, after a fashion. We're currently working on an example app and article for one of these techniques. For someone just starting out with Shiny, though, I'd recommend one of the other options.

messages.subject: Re: Which way is best to publish the Shiny App for company internal use?
messages.subject_clean: Which way is best to publish the Shiny App for company internal use?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ethan.

I came across a similar issue in the past 2 months. I work in a company with very restrictive rules regarding data security. So IT doesnt allow me to have any sort of linux virtual box... and all the user input data need to stay locally (my shiny app uses .txt files inputed by the user).

So basically I cant host my shiny app externally... and I cant install a shiny server locally.

I spend 1 month researching into this e the best solution was to use R-portable + shiny + bat file to start.

I installed r-portable, I editted the profile to install all libraries in the r-portable libraries folder and than I used a bat file so people can just double-click and start the application.

It works perfectly. I create a zip file with everything packed and leaved in some random folder in our intranet so everyone can acess...

Only problem is that r-portable seems to be available only in 32-bits which makes the app run slower than in r studio.

Best regards!
Rafael

messages.body_plain: (I'm working with Laz on a different email thread) I'm investigating some other solutions for you but one thing you can do, if your tag objects do not carry HTML dependencies or write to or make use of singleton() (and Laz's don't do any of that, I checked) you can wrap the large list of tag objects in htmltools::doRenderTags. Like so: fluidPage( doRenderTags( lapply(1:10000, function(i) { selectInput(... # whatever }) ) ) All this does is skip over the head, singleton, and dependency processing, and goes straight to the HTML rendering, returning the result as an HTML() object that can easily be included with the rest of the UI. This will save about 50% of the rendering time in your case, Laz. I'm working on something else to make it much faster than that, will check back in in an hour or two hopefully. messages.subject: Re: Issue with my app while creating a histogram form a selectInput
messages.subject_clean: Issue with my app while creating a histogram form a selectInput
messages.body_plain:
You're getting that error because of this:

  selectedCol<-reactive({
    as.numeric(tableData[,input$xcol])
  })

It should be tableData() instead of tableData:
  selectedCol<-reactive({
    as.numeric(tableData()[,input$xcol])
  })

After fixing that , there are other errors that your code raises. I suggest reading the debugging article to learn more about how to find and fix the problems:
  http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/debugging.html

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: Shiny HTML tags very slow
messages.subject_clean: Shiny HTML tags very slow
messages.body_plain: My other idea was to make a doRenderTags implementation in C++. I was far enough along that I decided to keep going. https://github.com/jcheng5/fasttags Replace doRenderTags() with fastrender(). You probably don't have to do %dopar% now; if that still makes a difference then it might be the creation of the graph that's taking time now, not the rendering, as fasttags should render all of the tags in much less than one second. With another day or two of effort I could probably get this to the point that it could fully replace renderTags, so htmltools rendering would just be fast without any more special tricks or caveats. > ^ > In file included from /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/Rcpp/include/RcppCommon.h:53:0, > from /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/Rcpp/include/Rcpp.h:27, > from fasttags.cpp:1: > /usr/include/c++/4.8/sstream:423:7: error: initializing argument 1 of ‘std::basic_ostringstream<_CharT, _Traits, _Alloc>::basic_ostringstream(std::ios_base::openmode) [with _CharT = char; I don't have that time to spare right at this moment but I've added it to our work backlog. > > > > > > On Fri, Nov 11, 2016 at 11:05 AM Laz C. Peterson wrote: > > > > We’re probably good for now, unless you have any more great ideas. > > > > > > > > But really, that sped it up so much I’m about ready to start foaming from the mouth. messages.body_plain: Besides generating the text, there are several other things a tag object *may* do. The most important is attaching HTML dependencies. That's why you can add, say, a data table using DT::dataTableOutput and not worry about where the supporting JavaScript and CSS files come from. There are also singleton() and tags$head() that are essentially an older attempt to support the same scenario that HTML dependencies now address. In any case, if forming the HTML by hand is working for you, you probably don't need to worry. If the aforementioned were going to cause problems for you, you'd likely notice. That said, it bums me out if the only reason you're avoiding tags is performance. I'll consider that another vote to make the fast C++ code path the default in a future release. messages.body_plain:
Another alternative can be to use shinyjs::onevent() to detect when enter/tab is pressed

library(shiny)
library(shinyjs)

ui <- fluidPage(
  useShinyjs(),
  textInput("text", "Enter text and hit Enter or Tab")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  onevent("keydown", "text", function(event) {
    if (event$keyCode == 13) {
      cat("Enter ")
      cat(input$text, "\n")
    }
    if (event$keyCode == 9) {
      cat("Tab ")
      cat(input$text, "\n")
    }
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

messages.subject_clean: how to get replacedata to work
messages.body_plain:
All,

I have a datatable and I would like to sequentially replace columns in the data based on the user's input - each user input choice will update a column from left to right.  I read the documentation which indicates the replacement table must have the same number of columns as the table.  I also looked at the example at the bottom of http://rstudio.github.io/DT/shiny.html - I have a minimal example below based on my understanding but the table data is not replaced.  In this example, I created two datatables one whose values are 2 and the other whose values are 4.  I would assume the datatable that is rendered would have values of 4 since the table whose values are 2 has been replaced.  What am I doing wrong?

Glenn

#
# This is a Shiny web application. You can run the application by clicking
# the 'Run App' button above.
#
# Find out more about building applications with Shiny here:
#
#    http://shiny.rstudio.com/
#

library(shiny)

# Define UI for application that draws a histogram
ui <- fluidPage(

DT::dataTableOutput("YieldAnalysis")
)
# Define server logic required to draw a histogram
DataTableOptions <- list(autowidth = TRUE,
                         searching = FALSE,
                         info = FALSE,
                         ordering = FALSE,
                         paging = FALSE)

  YieldTable <- datatable(data = array(data = 2,
                                       dim = c(9,7),
                                       dimnames = list(c("Scenario",
                                                         "Life CPR",
                                                         "Yield",
                                                         "Avg. Life",
                                                         "Modified Duration",
                                                         "First Payment",
                                                         "Last Payment",
                                                         "Curve Spread",
                                                         "Zero Vol Spread"),
                                                       rep("Scenario",7)))
                          ,options = DataTableOptions
                          ,rownames = TRUE
                          ,colnames = ""
                          ,escape = TRUE)

  YieldTableReplace <- array(data = 4, dim = c(9,7),
                             dimnames = list(c("Scenario",
                                               "Life CPR",
                                               "Yield",
                                               "Avg. Life",
                                               "Modified Duration",
                                               "First Payment",
                                               "Last Payment",
                                               "Curve Spread",
                                               "Zero Vol Spread"),
                                             rep("Scenario",7)))
server <- function(input, output) {

  output$YieldAnalysis <- renderDataTable({YieldTable})
  YieldAnalysisProxy <- dataTableProxy("YieldAnalysis")
  reactive({replaceData(YieldAnalysisProxy, YieldTableReplace)})

}

# Run the application
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

messages.subject: Invalidating downstream only if return value of a reactive expession changes
messages.subject_clean: Invalidating downstream only if return value of a reactive expession changes
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am writing a Shiny application where some long-running reactive computations depend on a data-frame that itself is the result of a reactive expression.

I would like the long-running computations to be triggered only if the *actual values* in the data-frame change, which might not always be the case (there can be changes in the inputs that do not trigger a change in the value of the data-frame).

I found that if the data-frame is returned from a reactive expression then downstream calculations are triggered once the reactive expression is invalidated, irrespective of whether the actual value returned by the reactive expression has changed. However, if I store it into a reactiveValue and subsequent calculations reference the reactiveValue object, then those are only triggered upon actual value change.

I prefer keeping everything a reactive expression and minimize the usage of reactiveValues if possible, so I was wondering if there was a way of using reactive expressions and still trigger downstream invalidation only if the actual value returned by the reactive expression changes.

Below is a minimal example that reproduces this behavior, when changing the input, only the reactive expression is re-triggered as shown by the console output:

```
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(

  title = 'reactive() vs reactiveValue()',

 sliderInput("test","Test",1,10,1),
  h3("The below numbers will not change:"),
  textOutput("test_1"),
  textOutput("test_2")
)

server <- shinyServer(
  function(input, output,session) {
    constant_val <- reactiveValues(val=1)

    observeEvent({input$test},
                 constant_val$val <- input$test^0)

    output$test_1 = renderText({
            print('re-running expensive computation with reactiveValue...')
            constant_val$val
    })

    constant_val2 <- reactive({
      input$test^0
    })

    output$test_2 = renderText({
      print('re-running expensive computation with reactive()...')
      constant_val2()
    })
})

shinyApp(ui,server)
```

Thank you very much for the help and apologies if this question has already been answered, I could not find any relevant references online.

Best regards,

Andras

messages.subject: Re: HeatMaps in Shiny
messages.subject_clean: HeatMaps in Shiny
messages.body_plain:
I had the same problem and use the following solution to be more responsive:

1) make the heatmap with the raster package (variable is in xyz below, example with US coordinates)
2) display the raster image in leaflet

1)
    make.heatmap <- reactive({
        heatm <- cbind(xyz()$LON,xyz()$LAT,xyz()$count)
        colnames(heatm) <- c('X', 'Y', 'Z')
        heatm.extent <- extent(-125,-60,20,50)
        heatm.raster <- raster(heatm.extent,ncol=650,300)
        heat.map <- rasterize(heatm[,1:2],heatm.raster,heatm[,3],fun=sum)
        heat.map[] <- heat.map[] / max(values(heat.map),na.rm=TRUE)
        crs(heat.map) <- "+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +no_defs +ellps=WGS84 +towgs84=0,0,0"
        return(heat.map)
    })

2)
addRasterImage(make.heatmap(), colors = pal, opacity = 0.4, group = "Heatmap")

Hope that helps,
D.

messages.body_plain:
Following is a question that I have already posted on stackoverflow, but have not been able to get an answer. I would appreciate if the group members could help me with it. I am reproducing the question below. Here is the link to stackoverflow question <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/40540783/how-to-properly-concatenate-bidi-strings-in-r>

I want to add markup to (Urdu language) text that is written right to left. I am trying to use gsub for the purpose but everything I have tried so far does not produce the desired output
text <- "یہ جملہ ایک مثال کے لیے استعمال کیا جا رہا ہے"
pattern <- "کیا جا"
replaceWith <- paste0("<somemark>", pattern, "</somemark>")
gsub(pattern, replaceWith, text)

gsub returns the following
یہ جملہ ایک مثال کے لیے استعمال <somemark>کیا جا</somemark> رہا ہے

desired output .

 <https://i.stack.imgur.com/Q4RUB.png>

How can I acheive the desired output?

Note: I could not even properly typeset the desired output in my post, I had to rely on an image instead.

Update: Although mysub function below correctly concatenates the strings(in console), I continue to face the problem of incorrect order of text in shiny app.
mysub <- function(text, pattern){
beforePattern <- substr(text, 1, regexpr(pattern, text)[1]-1)
afterPattern <- substr(text, regexpr(pattern,text)[1] + nchar(pattern), nchar(text))
result <- paste(afterPattern, replaceWith, beforePattern)
result
}

messages.subject: Re: Debugging reactivity
messages.subject_clean: Debugging reactivity
messages.body_plain:
Joe, is there a way to retrieve the current value from the progress object?

~ Laz Peterson
Paravis, LLC

> On Oct 17, 2016, at 1:10 AM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
>

> Sorry I never replied to this. You can use the object-oriented progress API (see ?shiny::Progress). You should be able to start the progress as the session starts, and close it at some later time (I'm assuming there's some easy place in your code that you definitely know everything's done processing--if not, we can talk about how to introduce that).
>
> Here's an example:
>
>
> library(shiny)
>
> ui <- fluidPage(
>   sidebarLayout(
>     sidebarPanel(
>       uiOutput("ui1"),
>       uiOutput("ui2")
>     ),
>     mainPanel(
>       verbatimTextOutput("result")
>     )
>   )
> )
>
> server <- function(input, output, session) {
>
>   progress <- Progress$new(session)
>   progress$set(message = "Please wait...")
>
>   output$ui1 <- renderUI({
>     Sys.sleep(3)
>     numericInput("x", "x", 5)
>   })
>
>   output$ui2 <- renderUI({
>     req(input$x)
>     Sys.sleep(3)
>     numericInput("y", "y", input$x * 2)
>   })
>
>   output$result <- renderPrint({
>     req(input$x, input$y)
>
>     if (!is.null(progress)) {
>       progress$close()
>       progress <<- NULL
>     }
>
>     input$x * input$y
>   })
> }
>
> shinyApp(ui, server)
>
> On Thu, Oct 13, 2016 at 11:24 AM Laz Peterson <l...@paravis.net> wrote:
> > Joe, the profile trace was awesome!
> >
> > Dropped the load time almost 10 seconds ... Good stuff.
> >
> > Now, I'm not sure if this needs another topic, but how can I go about creating a single progress indicator that covers all of the renderUI items during app initialization?  We have probably 30-40 of them, each with their own withProgress indicator, so as you can imagine, there are quite a few of those indicators flying across the screen during this time.  Would be much better if we could consolidate that into one progress bar.
> >
> > What do you think?
> >
> > Thanks again for the great profiling information.  That's a huge huge help!
> > ~Laz
> >
> >
> > On Wednesday, October 12, 2016 at 3:42:09 PM UTC-7, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> > > First off, it's far easier to troubleshoot performance issues by reproducing them outside of Shiny Server, i.e. from within RStudio. If you simply can't do it anywhere but on Shiny Server, then you still have some options.
> > >
> > > 1) Use reactlog. This works for relatively small apps with not too many reactive expressions and outputs (the UI for the reactlog visualization tool doesn't scale well), and only in situations where the time is being lost in reactive expressions and outputs. You can enable this by putting the line "options(shiny.reactlog=TRUE)" at the top of app.R, then when viewing the app in the browser, hit Ctrl+F3 (or Cmd+F3 if you're on a Mac). If you're using Shiny v0.14, after you step through the "Running" (green) portion of a reactive expression or output, you'll see an elapsed time. Note that if an output A calls a reactive expression B, and A shows 310 milliseconds while B shows 290 milliseconds, it may be the case that A's time includes B's time (so A itself only spent 20 milliseconds on its non-B-related operations).
> > >
> > > 2) Collect a profile trace on the server, and load it into profvis. Call Rprof("path-to-somewhere-writable.Rprof", memory.profiling=TRUE) at the top of app.R, and then at some later point after everything has loaded (use an actionButton/observeEvent if you need to), call Rprof(NULL). Then download the .Rprof file to your local machine that's running RStudio, and use the profvis package to visualize it:
> > > profvis::profvis(prof_input = "file.Rprof")
> > >
> > > Or you can send me the file.Rprof and I'll see if I can make sense of it myself using profvis.
> > >
> > > On Wed, Oct 12, 2016 at 3:16 PM Laz Peterson <l...@paravis.net> wrote:
> > > > Joe,
> > > >
> > > > Your head is definitely in the right place ... We *DO NOT* need that many options in the checkboxGroupInput.  I have re-created the MySQL views so that we are sorting by "instance counts", and now the list of 2800+ is down to 764.  That number is something we can work with.  The amount of time it takes to process is now very minimal.
> > > >
> > > > And yes, you are very right ... The user experience really isn't very fun when you have a list of nearly 3000 options in a checkbox group input.  So that's something I'll take care of ... (Specifically, we don't need any options where there are 0 pieces of data associated!)
> > > >
> > > > Now, there are a couple other chunks of 3-4 seconds of time that is lost while loading the app. We would really like to troubleshoot this.
> > > >
> > > > I added a withProgress to each of the renderUI objects in the app, but the first chunk of time lost still does not give any clue as to which process is taking up all that CPU time.
> > > >
> > > > Any recommendation on the best way to approach that?
> > > >
> > > > Aside from troubleshooting the performance for each little bit of the entire code, another option would be to simply block user input and display an overlay message with "Loading ..." (and maybe a cute animated image) until the entire app is loaded. What are your thoughts on that one?
> > > >
> > > > Our biggest issue with our clients is that they continually say, "Oh, this isn't usable," or, "It crashes every time we use it."  But the fact is that they simply don't wait until things are ready.  I would really like to make sure they are unable to mess up the session, because that seems to be the first thing they do.
> > > >
> > > > With all that being said, it would also be very nice to have some sort of progress indicator that encompasses everything (all reactive and non-reactive functions that are going on) so that the user can at least feel like they know something is going on, and the progress there.
> > > >
> > > > How do Shiny users normally provide this type of function?
> > > >

messages.subject: Course recommender web app using shiny
messages.subject_clean: Course recommender web app using shiny
messages.body_plain: I am new to R language and Shiny app. I am planning on building a course recommender web application. Is it possible to use Shiny app for the same considering the large database of students and courses? A brief description of the web app is : Students should be able to fill in their details(field of interest, courses taken etc) and the web app should be able to give course recommendations for that student using appropriate algorithm.

messages.subject_clean: Debugging reactivity
messages.body_plain:
No, I don't think so. But you do have Progress$inc and shiny::incProgress to increment progress by a relative amount rather than setting it to an absolute value.

On Tue, Nov 15, 2016 at 8:41 AM Laz C. Peterson <l...@paravis.net> wrote:
> Joe, is there a way to retrieve the current value from the progress object?
>
>
> ~ Laz Peterson
> Paravis, LLC
>
> > On Oct 17, 2016, at 1:10 AM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> >
> > Sorry I never replied to this. You can use the object-oriented progress API (see ?shiny::Progress). You should be able to start the progress as the session starts, and close it at some later time (I'm assuming there's some easy place in your code that you definitely know everything's done processing--if not, we can talk about how to introduce that).
> >
> > Here's an example:
> >
> >
> > library(shiny)
> >
> > ui <- fluidPage(
> >   sidebarLayout(
> >     sidebarPanel(
> >       uiOutput("ui1"),
> >       uiOutput("ui2")
> >     ),
> >     mainPanel(
> >       verbatimTextOutput("result")
> >     )
> >   )
> > )
> >
> > server <- function(input, output, session) {
> >
> >   progress <- Progress$new(session)
> >   progress$set(message = "Please wait...")
> >
> >   output$ui1 <- renderUI({
> >     Sys.sleep(3)
> >     numericInput("x", "x", 5)
> >   })
> >
> >   output$ui2 <- renderUI({
> >     req(input$x)
> >     Sys.sleep(3)
> >     numericInput("y", "y", input$x * 2)
> >   })
> >
> >   output$result <- renderPrint({
> >     req(input$x, input$y)
> >
> >     if (!is.null(progress)) {
> >       progress$close()
> >       progress <<- NULL
> >     }
> >
> >     input$x * input$y
> >   })
> > }
> >
> > shinyApp(ui, server)
> >
> > On Thu, Oct 13, 2016 at 11:24 AM Laz Peterson <l...@paravis.net> wrote:
> > > Joe, the profile trace was awesome!
> > >
> > > Dropped the load time almost 10 seconds ... Good stuff.
> > >
> > > Now, I'm not sure if this needs another topic, but how can I go about creating a single progress indicator that covers all of the renderUI items during app initialization?  We have probably 30-40 of them, each with their own withProgress indicator, so as you can imagine, there are quite a few of those indicators flying across the screen during this time.  Would be much better if we could consolidate that into one progress bar.
> > >
> > > What do you think?
> > >
> > > Thanks again for the great profiling information.  That's a huge huge help!
> > > ~Laz
> > >
> > >
> > > On Wednesday, October 12, 2016 at 3:42:09 PM UTC-7, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> > > > First off, it's far easier to troubleshoot performance issues by reproducing them outside of Shiny Server, i.e. from within RStudio. If you simply can't do it anywhere but on Shiny Server, then you still have some options.
> > > >
> > > > 1) Use reactlog. This works for relatively small apps with not too many reactive expressions and outputs (the UI for the reactlog visualization tool doesn't scale well), and only in situations where the time is being lost in reactive expressions and outputs. You can enable this by putting the line "options(shiny.reactlog=TRUE)" at the top of app.R, then when viewing the app in the browser, hit Ctrl+F3 (or Cmd+F3 if you're on a Mac). If you're using Shiny v0.14, after you step through the "Running" (green) portion of a reactive expression or output, you'll see an elapsed time. Note that if an output A calls a reactive expression B, and A shows 310 milliseconds while B shows 290 milliseconds, it may be the case that A's time includes B's time (so A itself only spent 20 milliseconds on its non-B-related operations).
> > > >
> > > > 2) Collect a profile trace on the server, and load it into profvis. Call Rprof("path-to-somewhere-writable.Rprof", memory.profiling=TRUE) at the top of app.R, and then at some later point after everything has loaded (use an actionButton/observeEvent if you need to), call Rprof(NULL). Then download the .Rprof file to your local machine that's running RStudio, and use the profvis package to visualize it:
> > > > profvis::profvis(prof_input = "file.Rprof")
> > > >
> > > > Or you can send me the file.Rprof and I'll see if I can make sense of it myself using profvis.

The amount of time it takes to process is now very minimal.
> > > > >

messages.body_plain:
Ok.

Reason I ask is because when we are incrementing progress through a group of reactive objects, somewhere (?) the increment value is somehow sending the progress bar to 1.

So I’m trying to figure out how it could even be doing that.

We are attempting to store/retrieve the current progress as an isolated reactive value each step of the way.  Everything adds up proper until the final reactive object, where we start with a progress value of 0.51, and increment by 0.05.  For some reason, that shoots up the progress bar to 100% on that first increment, but I can’t figure out how.  I was hoping to check the progress object’s current value before and after the increment just to verify where it’s at.

Any thoughts on how I can troubleshoot that one?

~ Laz Peterson
Paravis, LLC

messages.subject: Re: Detecting a mobile user
messages.subject_clean: Detecting a mobile user
messages.body_plain:
For anyone who is interested:

We are using the following JS to detect mobile:

function isMobile(){
try{document.createEvent('TouchEvent'); return true;}
catch(e){return false;}
}

I know that isn’t fool-proof, but it serves the purpose.

With that, we are then assigning a Shiny input binding either 0 or 1 based off of the isMobile() data.

Works like a charm.

~ Laz Peterson
Paravis, LLC

>
> ~ Laz Peterson

messages.body_plain:
Yes, it was actually a bit frustrating to put together — ha ha … I’ll get you some complete code to view the issue by sometime tomorrow.  On a roll with this app right now … :-)

I resorted to simply using Progress$set to “reset” the value to the current progress stored in the reactive value immediately after entering into a new reactive object.  As it goes, each time there is a Progress$inc, it also updates the reactive value as well.  Probably a lot of extra processing overhead there, but it definitely works now.

As I was trying to learn more about working with the progress objects — and this is the main reason for initially asking my question — it seems that we could really have a proper handle on the progress through multiple reactive objects if there was a way to query the progress object’s current value.  But if that’s not the intended use, then I’ll just leave it right there!

I’ll send a code tomorrow AM so you can see the behavior of Progress$inc through the reactive objects.

Thanks Joe!

~ Laz Peterson
Paravis, LLC

>
> I resorted to simply using Progress$set to “reset” the value to the current progress stored in the reactive value immediately after entering into a new reactive object.  As it goes, each time there is a Progress$inc, it also updates the reactive value as well.  Probably a lot of extra processing overhead there, but it definitely works now.
>
> As I was trying to learn more about working with the progress objects — and this is the main reason for initially asking my question — it seems that we could really have a proper handle on the progress through multiple reactive objects if there was a way to query the progress object’s current value.  But if that’s not the intended use, then I’ll just leave it right there!
>
> I’ll send a code tomorrow AM so you can see the behavior of Progress$inc through the reactive objects.
>
> Thanks Joe!
>
> ~ Laz Peterson
> Paravis, LLC

I'm having an issue with my Shiny app. When I launch the app, it loads the page fine. However, it just sits for about 10 seconds doing something.

The server eats up its allotted 25% CPU for the whole time, but when I trace activity, it shows nothing happening until the last split second, where it executes the optimization algorithm and then outputs the result.

I know it isn't my optimization because when I reduce the number of iterations from 500 to 10, it made no change in the load time. Not only that, I have a loading bar to show when the server status is "busy," and this bar doesn't show up for the first 10 seconds when I launch the app, but then briefly shows before the data is displayed. If I change the optimization parameters, it does the calculation in less than a second and updates. It is ONLY when I initially connect to the page that it takes forever to run anything. All my inputs show up, but anything rendering an output$... from the server will not calculate.

Anyone know what is causing this hang-up?

messages.body_plain:
https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/213733868-Running-Shiny-Server-with-a-Proxy was a useful setup guide.

But I still have some problems when trying to reach my app through a corp. proxy (I don't have much details about its configuration).

First experiment

-----------------------

I first tried a simple shiny-server on port 80 (on an external AWS host), without nginx/apache. Everything was working fine from home, but was crashing behind my corp. proxy: "Error: WebSocket closed".

Second experiment

----------------------------

Then I added an nginx over 443 (not 80) on the AWS host, as described in setup guide.

Now seems to work with IE through https, but not with firefox.

I also increased timeout:
app_init_timeout 120;
app_idle_timeout 20;

and tried

disable_protocols websocket xdr-polling;

(which seems not to work, according to browser console which still mentions socksjs and some XDR !)

Third experiment

------------------------

use 45-day eval of shiny-server-pro: now https is also working on firefox (and still IE), but basic http still not working for IE or firefox.

I am not skilled in web protocols, so these results are really confusing for me...

Any idea ?

Regards,

Yann.

This works for relatively small apps with not too many reactive expressions and outputs (the UI for the reactlog visualization tool doesn't scale well), and only in situations where the time is being lost in reactive expressions and outputs. You can enable this by putting the line "options(shiny.reactlog=TRUE)" at the top of app.R, then when viewing the app in the browser, hit Ctrl+F3 (or Cmd+F3 if you're on a Mac). If you're using Shiny v0.14, after you step through the "Running" (green) portion of a reactive expression or output, you'll see an elapsed time. Note that if an output A calls a reactive expression B, and A shows 310 milliseconds while B shows 290 milliseconds, it may be the case that A's time includes B's time (so A itself only spent 20 milliseconds on its non-B-related operations).

messages.body_plain:
Wow, that's a bug. Do you mind filing a github issue please? Thanks!

On Thu, Nov 17, 2016 at 1:50 PM Laz C. Peterson <l...@paravis.net> wrote:
> Joe,
>
> As I’ve been going through this preparing you a code, the issue happens when I use Progress$set(detail=“xxx”) without any value there (just to update the detail message).  It puts it all the way up to 1.  After removing the lines where I was simply using Progress$set() to update the detail, it seems to be ok.
>
> By default, when using set, does the value equal 1?
>
>
> ~ Laz Peterson
> Paravis, LLC
>

> > > >
> > > > I resorted to simply using Progress$set to “reset” the value to the current progress stored in the reactive value immediately after entering into a new reactive object.  As it goes, each time there is a Progress$inc, it also updates the reactive value as well.  Probably a lot of extra processing overhead there, but it definitely works now.
> > > >
> > > > As I was trying to learn more about working with the progress objects — and this is the main reason for initially asking my question — it seems that we could really have a proper handle on the progress through multiple reactive objects if there was a way to query the progress object’s current value.  But if that’s not the intended use, then I’ll just leave it right there!

> > > > Thanks Joe!

> > > > > > > > > Sorry I never replied to this. You can use the object-oriented progress API (see ?shiny::Progress). > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Here's an example:
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > library(shiny)

> > > > > > > > >   sidebarLayout(
> > > > > > > > >     sidebarPanel(
> > > > > > > > >       uiOutput("ui1"),
> > > > > > > > >       uiOutput("ui2")
> > > > > > > > >     ),

> > > > > > > > >     )
> > > > > > > > >   )
> > > > > > > > > )

> > > > > > > > >

> > > > > > > > >   progress$set(message = "Please wait...")

> > > > > > > > >     Sys.sleep(3)
> > > > > > > > >     numericInput("x", "x", 5)
> > > > > > > > >   })
> > > > > > > > >

> > > > > > > > >     req(input$x)

> > > > > > > > >     req(input$x, input$y)
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >     if (!is.null(progress)) {
> > > > > > > > >       progress$close()
> > > > > > > > >       progress <<- NULL
> > > > > > > > >     }
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >     input$x * input$y
> > > > > > > > >   })
> > > > > > > > > }

> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > 1) Use reactlog. This works for relatively small apps with not too many reactive expressions and outputs (the UI for the reactlog visualization tool doesn't scale well), and only in situations where the time is being lost in reactive expressions and outputs. You can enable this by putting the line "options(shiny.reactlog=TRUE)" at the top of app.R, then when viewing the app in the browser, hit Ctrl+F3 (or Cmd+F3 if you're on a Mac). If you're using Shiny v0.14, after you step through the "Running" (green) portion of a reactive expression or output, you'll see an elapsed time. Note that if an output A calls a reactive expression B, and A shows 310 milliseconds while B shows 290 milliseconds, it may be the case that A's time includes B's time (so A itself only spent 20 milliseconds on its non-B-related operations).
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > 2) Collect a profile trace on the server, and load it into profvis. Call Rprof("path-to-somewhere-writable.Rprof", memory.profiling=TRUE) at the top of app.R, and then at some later point after everything has loaded (use an actionButton/observeEvent if you need to), call Rprof(NULL). messages.subject: ggedit: interactive ggplot aesthetic and theme editor
messages.subject_clean: ggedit: interactive ggplot aesthetic and theme editor
messages.body_plain:
Hi

r-bloggers post <https://www.r-bloggers.com/ggedit-interactive-ggplot-aesthetic-and-theme-editor/>

ggedit <https://github.com/metrumresearchgroup/ggedit> is a package that helps users bridge the gap between making a plot and getting all of those pesky plot aesthetics just right, all while keeping everything portable for further research and collaboration.

ggedit is powered by a Shiny gadget <http://shiny.rstudio.com/> where the user inputs a ggplot plot object or a list of ggplot objects. You can run ggedit directly from the console from the Addin menu within RStudio.

The gadget returns a list containing 4 elements
updatedPlots
List containing updated ggplot objects
updatedLayers
For each plot a list of updated layers (ggproto) objects
Portable object
updatedLayersElements
For each plot a list elements and their values in each layer
Can be used to update the new values in the original code
updatedThemes
For each plot a list of updated theme objects
Portable object
If the user doesn’t edit the theme updatedThemes will not be returned
After you finish editing the plots the natural progression is to use them in the rest of the script. In ggedit there is the function rgg (remove and replace ggplot). Using this function you can chain into the original code changes to the plot without multiplying script needlessly.

messages.subject_clean: Integration of Shiny into a wordpress site feasable?
messages.body_plain:
This is probably no longer relevant to your problems, but considering I had spent quite some time to get the iframe for my shiny-app to resize correctly, I'm posting this answer for future reference. My setup is the following: I have a free shinyapps.io account and wanted to have a nice URL (instead of the ugly www.username.shinyapps.io/appname one) so I put up a website that basically just displays the shiny-app using an iframe. Thankfully, other people have been developing the necessary tools to do this (a big thanks to David Bradshaw ). Download iframe-resizer from his website! First, you have to set up the website which will point to the shiny-app. For this I simply modified one of the templates provided by David to look like this, the relevant parts are highlighted:
Make sure that all the necessary scripts ( ie8.polyfils.min.js, iframeResizer.min.js, downloaded from the iframe-resizer website ) are located within the same folder as the html-file, or to adjust the paths accordingly. Next, you will have to include a line of code in your Shiny-app and create a folder "www". Create a folder called "www" in the main directory of your shiny-app (where app.R or your server.R and UI.R are located). Move the iframeResizer.contentWindow.min.js script into that folder. Now, add the following line of code to the main Panel (or equivalent) of your app, like this: mainPanel( tags$body(tags$script(src="iframeResizer.contentWindow.min.js")), ...other stuff... ) And that's it. The iframe should automatically adjust its height to the size of the content inside the shiny-app, and the shiny-app will adjust to the width of the window. messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am a therapist and R user as well. I am developing a professional Wordpress website. From this website, I would like my customers to register, then to be able to record and monitor some personal information through a Shiny application.

The most important for me : I need my Shiny application to be very secured to warranty the identity and private information provided by my customers.

The idea that I have is inspired by the following post (https://groups.google.com/d/topic/shiny-discuss/3XM2mHuzqRs/discussion), enabling to pass parameters to Shiny from a website, after the customer logged in to the wordpress website. Both my Wordpress site and shiny app would be hosted on the same server like Amazon EC2 or DigitalOcean to facilitate the transfer of information between Wordpress and Shiny.

I wanted to ask you your feeling about this idea. Do you think it is enough secure, so that there is a limited risk for my customer information to be intercepted while some data are transferred between Wordpress and Shiny? Would you have any other solutions or ideas, excluding developing my application on a Shiny pro server, which is too much expensive for me?

Thanks in advance for your advice

Kind regards

Clem

messages.subject: Re: What is the best way to add a javascript in shiny when DOM is already loaded?
messages.subject_clean: What is the best way to add a javascript in shiny when DOM is already loaded?
messages.body_plain:
Hello Pablo —

What we do for our Shiny apps is we create an htmlOutput() that receives the JS raw script (text) as HTML() after every necessary part is loaded.

Create the output object with req(), and then place all of the date inputs you are creating with datepicker within that req() function.  That way, the JS will not output the JS until all of those datepicker inputs specified within req() have been created.

I’m not a pro at this, so there is probably a better way.  But that should get you on a start.

~ Laz Peterson
Paravis, LLC

shinyServer(function(input, output){

fdata <- reactive({
infile <- input$file1
if (is.null(infile)) {
return(NULL)
}
read.csv(infile$datapath,header=T,col.names=c("Week","product_id","loc_id","Sales"))
})

# choose_product <- reactive({
# unique(fdata()$product_id)
# })
#
# choose_store <- reactive({
# unique(sort(fdata()$loc_id))
# })

output$select_product <- renderUI({
selectInput('xcol', "Select Product", unique(sort(fdata()$product_id)))
})

output$select_store <- renderUI({
selectInput('ycol', "Select Store", unique(sort(fdata()$loc_id)))
})

mystats <- function(x, na.omit=TRUE)
{
if (na.omit) x <- x[!is.na <http://is.na>(x)]
m <- mean(x)
n <- length(x)
s <- sd(x)
min <- min(x)
max <- max(x)
med<-median(x)
UC <- m+3*s
LC <- m-3*s
return(c(n=n,median=med, mean=m, stdev=s,min = min, max=max, UC=UC, LC=LC))
}

dm<-reactive({

Sales<-fdata()
SubSales<-subset(Sales,product_id==input$xcol & loc_id==input$ycol, select = c("Week","product_id","loc_id","Sales"))
SubSales$Week<-as.Date(SubSales$Week, format = "%d-%m-%y")
len.data<-length(SubSales$Week)
min.data<-SubSales$Week[1]
max.data<-SubSales$Week[len.data]
all.data<-as.data.frame(seq(min.data,max.data, by = "week"))
colnames(all.data)<-c("Week")
SubSales<-merge(all.data,SubSales,by.x ="Week",by.y = "Week",all = T)
SubSales=SubSales[-grep(53,week(SubSales$Week)),]

##### Storing as a List
var_dm<-as.list(mystats(SubSales$Sales))

##### Imputing missing values
SubSales$Sales[is.na <http://is.na>(SubSales$Sales==TRUE)] <- var_dm$mean

##### Removing outliers
SubSales$Sales[(SubSales$Sales>var_dm$UC)] <- var_dm$UC

var_week <- week(SubSales$Week)[1]
var_year <-year(SubSales$Week[1])
var_split=0.9
train_len=round(nrow(SubSales)*var_split)
test_len=nrow(SubSales)
var_len=round((test_len-train_len))
var_maxDate <- max(SubSales$Week)

#### Training Set
training<-slice(SubSales,1:train_len)
#### Testing Set
testing<-slice(SubSales,train_len+1:test_len)

ts_Sales<-ts(SubSales$Sales,freq=52,start=c(var_year,var_week))
tlist<-list(testing$Sales,ts_Sales,var_maxDate)
return(tlist)
})

funcfcast<-function(a,b,c,d,fit)
{
if(input$var=="STLF")
fcast<-stlf(b,h=d,lambda=0)
else
fcast<-forecast(fit,h=d)

dfcast<-data.frame(fcast)
x<-data.frame(seq(as.Date(c+7), by = "week", length.out = d))
ffcast<-as.data.frame(cbind(x,round(dfcast$Point.Forecast,digits = 2),round(dfcast$Lo.95,digits = 2),round(dfcast$Hi.95,digits = 2)))
names(ffcast)<-c("Week","Forecast","Lo-95","Hi-95")
facc<-accuracy(fcast$mean,a)

fplot<-plot_ly() %>%
add_lines(x = time(b), y = b,
color = I("black"), name = "observed") %>%
add_ribbons(x = time(fcast$mean), ymin = fcast$lower[,2], ymax = fcast$upper[,2],
color = I("gray80"), name = "95% confidence") %>%
add_lines(x = time(fcast$mean), y = fcast$mean, color = I("blue"), name = "prediction")

flist<-list(facc,ffcast,fplot)
return(flist)
}

getDataModel <- reactive({

dmsales<-dm()
if (input$var=="Arima")
{
fit <- auto.arima(dmsales[[2]])
}

else if (input$var=="Linear Model")
{
fit <- tslm(dmsales[[2]]~trend+season)
}
else if (input$var=="STLF")
{
fit <- stlf(dmsales[[2]])
}
else if (input$var=="Basic exponential smoothing")
{
fit <- HoltWinters(dmsales[[2]], beta = FALSE, gamma = FALSE)
}
else if (input$var=="Double exponential smoothing")
{
fit <- HoltWinters(dmsales[[2]], gamma = FALSE)
}
else
{
fit <- HoltWinters(dmsales[[2]])
}

funcfcast(dmsales[[1]],dmsales[[2]],dmsales[[3]],input$ahead,fit)

})

getbestforecast<-reactive({

dmsales<-dm()
############ Calculating Mape for different methods and storing in a variable########
fit1 <- auto.arima(dmsales[[2]])
fit1fcast<-forecast(fit1,h=input$ahead)
ArAcc<-as.data.frame(accuracy(fit1fcast$mean,dmsales[[1]]))

fit2 <- tslm(dmsales[[2]]~trend+season)
fit2fcast<-forecast(fit2,h=input$ahead)
LmAcc<-as.data.frame(accuracy(fit2fcast$mean,dmsales[[1]]))

fit3 <- stlf(dmsales[[2]])
fit3fcast<-stlf(dmsales[[2]],h=input$ahead,lambda=0)
STLFacc<-as.data.frame(accuracy(fit3fcast$mean,dmsales[[1]]))

fit4 <- HoltWinters(dmsales[[2]], beta = FALSE, gamma = FALSE)
fit4fcast<-forecast(fit4,h=input$ahead)
Hw1Acc<-as.data.frame(accuracy(fit4fcast$mean,dmsales[[1]]))

fit5 <- HoltWinters(dmsales[[2]], gamma = FALSE)
fit5fcast<-forecast(fit5,h=input$ahead)
HW2Acc<-as.data.frame(accuracy(fit5fcast$mean,dmsales[[1]]))

fit6 <- HoltWinters(dmsales[[2]])
fit6fcast<-forecast(fit6,h=input$ahead)
HW3Acc<-as.data.frame(accuracy(fit6fcast$mean,dmsales[[1]]))

MAPE<-c(ArAcc$MAPE,LmAcc$MAPE,Hw1Acc$MAPE,HW2Acc$MAPE,HW3Acc$MAPE,STLFacc$MAPE) #// All Models' Mape
MAPE<-round(MAPE,digits=2)
ModelForecast<-c("Arima","LM","Basic exponential smoothing","Double exponential smoothing","Triple exponential smoothing","stlf") #// Model Names
MinMape<-sort(MAPE)
min_mape<-MinMape[1]
Minmatch<-match(min_mape,MAPE)
var1 <- ModelForecast[Minmatch]
var2<-switch(var1,
"Arima" = forecast(auto.arima(dmsales[[2]]),h=input$ahead),
"LM" = forecast(tslm(dmsales[[2]]~trend+season),h=input$ahead),
"Basic exponential smoothing" = forecast(HoltWinters(dmsales[[2]],beta = FALSE,gamma = FALSE),h=input$ahead),
"Double exponential smoothing" = forecast(HoltWinters(dmsales[[2]],gamma = FALSE),h=input$ahead),
"Triple exponential smoothing" = forecast(HoltWinters(dmsales[[2]]),h=input$ahead),
"stlf" =stlf(dmsales[[2]],h=input$ahead,lambda=0))

var2<-as.data.frame(var2)
y<-data.frame(seq(as.Date(dmsales[[3]]+7), by = "week", length.out = input$ahead))
bfcast<-as.data.frame(cbind(y,round(var2$`Point Forecast`,digits = 2),round(var2$`Lo 95`,digits = 2),round(var2$`Hi 95`,digits = 2)))
names(bfcast)<-c("Week","Forecast","Lo-95","Hi-95")

bflist<-list(min_mape,bfcast,var1)
return(bflist)
})

output$table <- renderDataTable({

if(is.null(fdata()))
{return ()}

data<-fdata()
data <- data[data$product_id == input$xcol,]
data <- data[data$loc_id == input$ycol,]
data
},rownames=FALSE, options = list(searching = FALSE))

output$bfcast<-renderDataTable({
new <- getbestforecast()
new[[2]]

},options = list(searching = FALSE,paging = FALSE))

output$mape<-renderPrint({
new <- getbestforecast()
new[[1]]
})

output$mod<-renderPrint({
new <- getbestforecast()
new[[3]]
})

output$facc<-renderPrint({
new <- getDataModel()
new[[1]]
})

output$fplot <- renderPlotly({
new <- getDataModel()
new[[3]]
})

output$fcast<-renderDataTable({
new <- getDataModel()
new[[2]]
},options = list(searching = FALSE,paging = FALSE))

output$dData <- downloadHandler(
filename = function() { paste(input$xcol,'_',input$ycol, '.csv', sep='') },
content = function(file) {
write.csv(getDataModel()[[2]], file,row.names = F)
}
)

})

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I keep strugling with a "disconnected from server" error in my shiny app while running it on shiny.io <http://shiny.io> server. Due to the characteristics of the problem I can only come up with one possible cause namely that something goes wrong when server and client try to reconnect after the connection was lost. Is it possible that due to reconnecting, the vector "resp" somehow stores multiple or zero answers per OK button click ? The code looks like this:

observeEvent(input$OK,{
      if (input$OK > n  ){
         reac_vars$resp<-c(reac_vars$resp, input$survey)
      }
})

because:
-In the error log it sais that the length of the resp vector is not correct (different amount of answers stored than questions asked ). That is why my computations fail and the app crashes.
-I never have this problem locally.
-I never have the problem myself online (on my computer, with a stable internet connection).
-Not everyone has the problem online (1 out of 5 people).
-I can see that reconnect happens in the log.

Kind regards,
Frits

messages.subject: Re: How to reset action button on changing menuItem in shinydashboard
messages.subject_clean: How to reset action button on changing menuItem in shinydashboard
messages.body_plain:
Aaghaz - in the Big Picture, you can read inputs but you can't write to them (and you can write to outputs but you can't read them) and the inputs on actionButtons increase by 1 each time you click them. So it's not possible to reset the actionButton's input value to zero.

On the other hand, you can both read and write global variables and reactive values. So you can keep track of the action button status by using one of those. Set up an observeEvent for each tab change and use those to reset the designated global or reactive to 0, In the observeEvent that reacts to actionButton clicks, increment the designated value.

As you gain more experience with Shiny, you'll probably figure out an even better way to accomplish what you're trying to do.

Tom

messages.subject: Re: can a radio button setting be changed progromatically
messages.subject_clean: can a radio button setting be changed progromatically
messages.body_plain:
Basel - there are two ways to do this. The simple one, which is the one you're probably looking for, is the Shiny function updateRadioButtons().

Alternatively, you can re-render the output the radio button is in. Assuming the initial value of the radio button is hard-coded and not a variable, that will also restore the buttons to their initial value. To force a re-render of the output, it needs to include something "reactive." Change that and the output will be re-rendered. The reactive value doesn't have to actually appear in the output, something like this will work:

output$xxx <- renderUI([
    x <- rv$render_xxx         # you don't have to actually use "x" for anything
   taglist(
      # what you want to render goes here
   )
})

messages.subject: Use isolate() with actionButton or not?
messages.subject_clean: Use isolate() with actionButton or not?
messages.body_plain:
In my shiny app, users give a year, date and weather station of which they want temperature data. Then they click an action button which generates a plot based on a selection of data according to the input.
I used to have no action button, but with each change in input the plot was remade and it all went extremely slow. I also got an error message which showed for 2 secs before the plot appeared. Sometimes first an empty plot showed for a few secs and then the right plot appeared. Lots of weird and slow stuff, so I decided to let the effect of changed input be delayed until a button is clicked.

In my server part of the app, the code for the plot before I had the button looked like this:
output$plotTemp <- renderPlot({
  importdata(input$jaartal)
  weerstation <- which(weerstations == input$weerstation)
  temperatuur(input$datums, weerstation)
})

importdata() and temperatuur() are functions I import via source(script.R) at the start of the app. They import and calculate temperature data and temperatuur() creates a ggplot at the end.

When I inserted the action button, called "button", the code looked like this:
inputJaar <- eventReactive(input$button, {input$jaartal})
inputDatum <- eventReactive(input$button, {input$datums})
inputStation <- eventReactive(input$button, {
  weerstation <- which(weerstations == input$weerstation)
})
output$plotTemp <- renderPlot({
  importdata(inputJaar())
  temperatuur(inputDatum(), inputStation())
})
I'm not sure if this is proper/clean programming. I have little experience and never used actionButton() before. All I know is that things still go very slow, but at least it doesn't recalculate with every change in input. Also the error or empty plot that showed for a few secs never appear again. That's a good start.

When I asked someone if it was possible to speed things up (or have cleaner code) they told me to use isolate(). I read help pages, saw a youtube video and read some blogs. But I can't grab the difference with my current code (except that it's shorter). Anyway, the code with isolate looks like this:
output$plotTemp <- renderPlot({
  input$button
  isolate({
    importdata(input$jaartal)
    weerstation <- which(weerstations == input$weerstation)
    temperatuur(input$datums, weerstation)
  })
})
I don't notice any changes in speed. The plot still only changes after I click the button, but the error that appeared a few secs before the plot in my first version now appears when I open the plot. It dissapears after I click the button. I don't want my users to see an error at the start, they'll think it's not working.
The error says: "x must be of length 1 or 2". I tried to understand en avoid this before I came up with the actionbutton solution, but never found it.
Anyway, with the button but without isolate, it doesn't show, so I started to ignore it...

What's the difference between the 2nd and 3rd code? An explanation "for dummies" about using isolate or not with the actionbutton would also be very welcome.
Any other solutions or tips to improve my code? (good programming practices or so :) )

Thanks in advance!

Having seen this error message way too many times, I finally figured out that a "closure" is a function.  As a practical matter, it usually means you've forgotten to put parentheses after a function somewhere. In my case, it's almost always a reactive expression. So, for example, if you have:

x <- reactive (...)

when you want to use actually use x, you have say x()

Tom

messages.subject: Re: Use isolate() with actionButton or not?
messages.subject_clean: Use isolate() with actionButton or not?
messages.body_plain:
Either way is perfectly fine, whichever seems more intuitive to you.

If you want your isolate() code to not throw an error, replace this line:

input$button

with this:

req(input$button)

This will have the effect of cancelling the plot if the button has never been pressed (as is the case when your app first loads). See http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/req.html for more info.

messages.subject: App disconnects on sleep
messages.subject_clean: App disconnects on sleep
messages.body_plain:
No one else seems to complain about this, which makes me think I'm the only one with this issue.

My shiny app (on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>) shuts down when my laptop goes to sleep.  I get the dreaded gray screen.  Sure I could just refresh it, but it's annoying because every time it requires reuploading data and changing inputs.

I've been told by support that "unfortunately this is due to Chrome and Safari's behavior around XMLHttpRequests and not something we can control."

Has anyone found any workaround at all?  Presumably this should happen with shiny server as well.

I can't be the only one ...
